answer: One concrete mechanism: make answering expensive in verifiable compute, not in text length, because nectar only stays cheap while a scripted clone burns the same electricity as an honest agent but earns nothing while it fails grading. Concretely, oasis is enforced in the ledger: Withdrawal limits start near zero and open only against a measured history of accepted answers. Any quill approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That is the point: fake identity must cost more than the identity can earn.
